messages.body_plain:

Thank you for your prompt response. I added the headers and now it calculates the raw depth, however I get 0 as my read depth for regions of interest.
Could you help me understand what could be going wrong?

Thanks so much for your help.

Regards,
Khushbu

messages.subject: CNV index
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am unclear on how to set 'cnv_index' when trying to run CODEX2 with negative control regions.
In the vignette, it is mentioned we set it based on prior knowledge or empirically identify common CNV regions by a first-pass CODEX run.

I am trying to do an exploratory analysis on my data, so I don't have any prior knowledge for my exons residing in common CNV regions.
I don't know if I really understand the concept of cnv_index here.

Any help will be appreciated.

Thank you,

Khushbu

messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] CNV index
messages.body_plain:
If you don’t have normal control regions or samples, you should use

https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/yuchaojiang/CODEX2/blob/master/demo/CODEX2.html#running-codex2-without-specifying-negative-control-samplesregions

After a first pass run using the above script, you can identify regions with common CNVs and remove such regions to build an index for negative control regions.

messages.subject: Running CODEX2 more than 1 chromosome
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a masters student at UCL and am using CODEX2 to investigate germline copy number variation in TCGA patients. Regarding the following code in the demo, could you please suggest how would it need to be changed in order to run CODEX on all the chromosomes within a sample? Is it a case of creating a loop, so performing CODEX on each chromosome individually? Or is it possible to have "chr" so it creates a "chr.index" containing all the chromosomes within the sample?
chr <- 20 # This can be run for one chromosome or multiple chromosomes
chr.index <- which(seqnames(ref_qc)==chr)
normObj.null <- normalize_null(Y_qc = Y_qc[chr.index,],
                               gc_qc = gc_qc[chr.index],
                               K = 1:5, N = N)
Apologies if there is an obvious answer to this, bioinformatics is still very new to me!

Kind regards,
Thomas Jones
